issues.detail: The Hebrew 'וְכָל הָרֵעַ לְאִישׁ מַתָּן' means 'and every friend of a man of gifts' (i.e., everyone who is a friend of a generous man), but the Vietnamese renders it as 'and every acquaintance is a friend of the one who gives gifts,' changing the meaning: the Hebrew says all who are friends belong to the giver, not that all acquaintances become friends of the giver. The phrase 'hā-rēa' (the friend) is rendered as 'kẻ quen biết' (acquaintance), and the construct 'l'îsh mattān' (of a man of gifts) is turned into a predicate 'đều là bạn hữu của người hay ban tặng' (are friends of the giver), altering the relationship.
